config.grain_rationale: Each record is one QBCC licence held by a licensee (Licence Number + Licence Grade + Licence Class Type identify the licence; _id is the CKAN row id). The business participant is the licensee named in 'Licensee Name'. Licence-level attributes (grade, class, financial category) describe the licence, not the entity. The register is a flat export that never distinguishes a registered legal name from a trading name, so 'Licensee Name' is mapped only to entity.legal_name: for 'Company' rows it is the registered company name (corroborated by a checksum-valid ACN and PTY LTD suffixes), for 'Individual' rows it is the natural person who is the licensee. No trading name is claimed because the source provides none.

record_id.rationale: CKAN datastore row id; 508/508 distinct across the discovery partition and unique in held-out validation, so it identifies the licence record. Licence Number is not unique (506 distinct vs 508 rows), so it cannot be used alone.

fields.rationale: Single licensee-name column in a government licence register, mapped in full with no suffix heuristic and no suppression. Previous revision emitted only company-suffixed names here (7% coverage) and pushed personal names to trading_name; the reviewer rejected that split. An individual licensee is the natural person holding the licence, so its name belongs in legal_name rather than being dropped or relabelled as a trading name.

Direct source column in '99 999 999 999' shape; ABN checksum valid on 99.6% of discovery rows and 99.0% of held-out rows (1 and 6 rejections respectively). The abn transform strips separators and refuses to emit a checksum-invalid value, so bad source data surfaces as a counted error instead of a fabricated ABN. The residual ~1% rejections are reported honestly, not hidden.
All present values are '999 999 999'; 100% ACN checksum-valid in both discovery (34/34) and held-out (76/76) with zero errors. ACN is never derived from the ABN.

The source states the licensee type directly and 'C' -> company is well supported (ACN present, PTY LTD names). 'I' is deliberately NOT mapped to sole_trader after the reviewer rejected that inference (an individual licensee may be a partner or trust principal); 'I' rows therefore resolve to the ontology default 'unknown' rather than a guess.
Free-text single-line business address ending in state + postcode, e.g. '15 radiata pl Peregian Springs QLD 4573'. Passed through as stated by the source with whitespace normalisation only.

All addresses follow '<street> <suburb> <STATE> <postcode>'; the state token immediately before the trailing postcode is extracted and normalised by the state op (unknown -> OTHER). Reviewer verdict 'ok'; 1080/1092 held-out rows emitted with zero errors.
Trailing numeric token of the address, validated by the postcode op (AU 4-digit, NT re-pad). Reviewer verdict 'ok'; 100% coverage with zero errors in both partitions.
QBCC licence number uniquely identifies the licence per publisher guidance.
Licence type descriptor (Individual/Company) is the publisher's licence category wording; per publisher evidence it does not establish legal form.
Published grade of the licence, e.g. Trade Contractor Licence or Nominee Supervisor.
Published licence class preserved in QBCC terminology, e.g. Carpentry or Plumbing and Drainage, covering 57 distinct classes.

constants.rationale: Queensland Building and Construction Commission register; every address carries a QLD state code and an AU 4-digit postcode. Inferred from the publisher and address format rather than a source column, so confidence is moderate and flagged for review.

unmapped.reason: CKAN datastore row id for the licence record, not a business identifier; used only as record_id.

Only address.full, address.state and address.postcode are taken from this column. address.locality is deliberately not mapped: the reviewer found the street-type-suffix heuristic brittle (missed COURT, ESPLANADE, unit-numbered and street-less addresses) and it covered only ~58-60% of held-out rows. Emitting no locality leaves the value absent rather than wrong.
Licence financial category ('Self Certification - Trade' for 100% of discovery rows), a property of the licence, not of the entity.
Code form of the licence financial category ('SCT1'); licence attribute, single-valued in the discovery partition, not an entity field.

config.notes: REVISION after review. Advertised as CSV but the resource is a CKAN datastore_search API JSON envelope (starts '{"help":'), so format=json with record_path 'result.records'. No date column exists in the records: observation.observed_at falls back to resource last-modified metadata and no valid_from/valid_to can be supplied. Fixes for the reviewer's verdicts: (1) entity.trading_name REMOVED ('wrong' verdict - a personal licensee name is not a trading name, and for companies it duplicated the legal name); (2) the suffix-based legal_name heuristic REMOVED - 'Licensee Name' is now mapped in full to entity.legal_name (coverage 100%, no suppression, no guessing), which also resolves the 'doubtful' over-suppression of individual licensees; (3) entity.entity_type now maps only 'C'->company and lets 'I' fall to the ontology default 'unknown', removing the rejected 'I'->sole_trader inference; (4) address.locality REMOVED as brittle ('doubtful'), so address output is full/state/postcode only, all of which the reviewer rated 'ok'. Retained deliberately: entity.abn and entity.acn (direct, checksum-validated source columns rated 'ok'; ABN keeps a reported ~1% checksum rejection rather than hiding it) and address.country 'AU' at reduced confidence 0.8 and flagged. Open coverage gaps for a human: entity.trading_name (no trading name exists in this source), entity.status (no status column - register membership implies current licensing but that is inferred), entity.industry_code (no ANZSIC; Licence Class Type is the nearest but non-conforming signal), address.locality (unparseable from the free-text address), and no date fields at all.

fields.reason: Licence Number is trimmed and emitted as context.licence.number, matching the ontology path for a publisher-assigned licence number.

Licence Type DESC holds the holder/licence type distinction (Individual vs Company), not a licence category or class of work. Mapping it to context.licence.category makes the category semantically the licence-holder form; the publisher evidence explicitly says the licence type does not establish legal form, and it is equally not the publisher's work category. This also collides with grade/class, which carry the real category information.
Licence Grade values (e.g. Trade Contractor Licence, Site Supervisor, Nominee Supervisor) are the published grade of the licence; trimmed and whitespace-collapsed text preserved verbatim.

The observed value 'Mechanical Services - Air-conditioning and Refrigeration (Unlimited De...' is truncated relative to the source 'Mechanical Services - Air-conditioning and Refrigeration (Unlimited Design)'. The class is not preserved in publisher wording, so this rule corrupts the value and violates the 'preserve the publisher wording' requirement of context.licence.class.

critic.summary: The four rules target the right ontology paths, but two are semantically or operationally defective. Rule 1 mis-serialises Licence Type DESC (a holder-form/derived entitlement type, per publisher evidence unable to establish legal form, let alone a licence category) as the licence category, so context.licence.category should not be populated from it. Rule 3's class value is truncated in output ('…(Unlimited De...'), which breaks the requirement to preserve the publisher's class wording. Rules 0 and 2 are correct, with number and grade emitted verbatim. No obvious ontology target was left unmapped: locational and financial-category columns have defensible reasons for exclusion, though 'Licensee Business Address' arguably belongs under address.* (already partially emitted) rather than being treated as unmapped.

fields.reason: Licence Number is trimmed and emitted verbatim as context.licence.number; all held-out values (54898, 1317628, 15074969, 705525) reproduce exactly, matching the publisher-assigned licence identifier scoped to the licence.

Licence Grade is copied verbatim (trim + whitespace collapse) to context.licence.grade; rare values such as 'Fire Occupational', 'Building Designer Licence' and 'Trade Contractor Licence - Fire Certifier' are preserved whole rather than coerced into an enum, which is correct for a publisher-wording grade field.

The rule claims verbatim preservation 'without whitespace rewriting so values are not truncated', but held-out row 11 emits 'Mechanical Services - Air-conditioning and Refrigeration (Unlimited De...' — the source value '... (Unlimited Design)' was truncated by the engine's default string length cap. The observation is silently corrupt and the rationale falsely asserts the class is preserved; the rule must configure a longer max-length/no-truncation so parenthetically qualified classes survive.

missed.reason: The dataset grain rationale explicitly states that 'Licensee Name' is mapped to entity.legal_name for company and individual rows, yet the mapping array contains no such rule (only three licence-context rules). The claimed core entity observation is therefore never emitted; this is the most important omission.

The grain rationale says Licence Type CODE is the machine value used for entity_type ('Individual'/'Company'), and the unmapped list defers to it, but no entity_type rule exists in the mapping. Without it the entity's legal form, which the publisher notes cannot be inferred from licence category, is unrecorded.

missed.suggested_target: address.full / address.state / address.postcode (and address.locality when derivable)
missed.reason: The unmapped note asserts that address.full, address.state and address.postcode are taken from this column, and that locality is deliberately withheld, but no address rule appears in the mapping. Either the address claims are absent entirely (unmapped note is inaccurate) or they should be added explicitly. Locality omission itself is a defensible precision choice, but it does not excuse the missing address coverage.

missed.source_path: Licensee ABN / ACN (if present in the register export)
missed.reason: The grain rationale relies on 'a checksum-valid ACN and PTY LTD suffixes' as corroboration for company rows, implying such columns exist; if present they are a publisher-authoritative business identifier and should not be left out.

critic.summary: All three mapped rules target the licence context and two (number, grade) are correctly verbatim, but rule_index 2 is wrong because the emitted class value is truncated ('(Unlimited De...'), falsifying its stated no-truncation guarantee and producing a corrupted rare-value observation. More seriously, the mapping is missing the entity-level rules its own grain rationale depends on — Licensee Name to entity.legal_name, Licence Type CODE to entity.entity_type, and the business address fields — while the unmapped notes describe those claims as if they were emitted. The dataset stays within licence-level scope and correctly avoids enum guessing on grade/class wording, but the entity side of the configuration is unimplemented.

publisher_evidence.notes: A licence may be held by an individual or company. The QBCC licence number identifies the licence. An ABN is issued separately for tax and trading purposes. A licence category does not by itself establish the holder's legal form.
The company application collects ACN, ABN and the licensee's business address. The business address is published in the licence register.
